name: Will Foundation Repair Stop Drywall Cracks From Returning?

mainEntity.name: Will foundation repair stop interior drywall cracks from coming back?
mainEntity.text: Will foundation repair stop interior drywall cracks from coming back?

acceptedAnswer.text: Interior drywall cracks often reappear when the underlying movement has not been corrected. If the foundation or framing is still shifting, cosmetic repairs such as tape, mud, and paint are only temporary. A foundation repair contractor should first determine whether the structure is stable or still active. If the problem is active, stabilization should come before any final interior finish repair. In Los Angeles County, seasonal moisture changes, settlement, and seismic influences can all contribute to recurring cracks. If the contractor recommends patching without addressing the foundation cause, the repair is likely incomplete. The right sequence is diagnosis, stabilization, then cosmetic restoration.
acceptedAnswer.description: It can, but only if the repair stops the underlying movement. If cracks are caused by active settlement, slope, or moisture-related soil changes, cosmetic patching will not prevent recurrence. A proper foundation repair contractor should stabilize the structure first, then recommend drywall repair after movement has been addressed. If the structure keeps moving, cracks may return.
